text:
Investigation 2026-05-11: shallow-cloned Netflix/bettertls into ~/GIT/bettertls. The upstream repo's test-suites/ tree contains exactly two test suites: 'nameconstraints' (tests how implementations handle SAN matching under name constraints) and 'pathbuilding' (chain-building tests). There is no 'dnsnames' or hostname-matching test suite in the upstream BetterTLS project. The premise of this bead (as filed by me during PKIX-fmtv.11.1 work) was incorrect — I extrapolated 'hostname-matching corpus' from the existence of bettertls's other suites without verifying.

Options considered:

(a) Vendor a subset of bettertls's nameconstraints suite for hostname-binding tests. Rejected — this suite is primarily about name-constraint enforcement (which lives in pkix-path, not pkix-identity), and x509-limbo Tier-2 already provides bettertls::nameconstraints coverage through pkix-difftest's existing harness.

(b) Hand-author a new hostname-matching corpus from scratch and check it in. Rejected — defeats the purpose of using an external corpus as independent oracle. The 26 unit tests + 18 integration tests already shipped in PKIX-fmtv.11.1 cover RFC 6125 §6.4 spec text exhaustively (exact match / wildcard rules / IDN / IP / SAN-missing / mixed-case scenarios), with pyca/cryptography as the independent oracle producing fixtures.

(c) Pull dnsnames-relevant testcases from the existing x509-limbo bettertls::nameconstraints corpus and project them onto verify_dns_name. Possible but only modest coverage gain over the spec-driven tests already in place, and the dispatch from name-constraints-test-shape to hostname-binding-target-shape would require harness adapter code that wouldn't pay back as a maintainable feature.

Closing as obsolete-on-investigation. The PKIX-fmtv.11.1 acceptance criterion 'bettertls corpus integration test passing' was vacuously not satisfiable; the substantive acceptance (RFC 6125 §6.4 implementation + comprehensive tests + clean clippy / fmt / docs / no_std / wasm32 builds) was satisfied.
